interest: Japanese insiders describe a Foreign Ministry dominated by European and China hands; a SCAP labor chief resigns, 1949.
keywords: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
overview: This decimal file (894.02, covering December 1947 to July 1949) documents the executive departments of the Japanese government under Allied Occupation, focusing primarily on the organization, staffing, and internal politics of the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Gaimusho) and the administration of labor policy within the General Headquarters of the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP). The primary component is a confidential December 1947 despatch and comprehensive organizational enclosure from Acting Political Adviser William J. Sebald analyzing the personnel, functions, and factional struggles of the Foreign Office, particularly the persistence of a pro-European diplomatic clique, neglect of American affairs, and the establishment of a diplomatic Training Institute. The file also includes a July 1949 confidential despatch reporting the resignation of Chester W. Hepler, Chief of SCAP's Labor Division, who stepped down over policy disagreements regarding SCAP's treatment of Japanese organized labor to take a post with the International Labor Organization in Geneva.

subfiles.about: A confidential despatch analyzing the internal organization, factional dynamics, pro-European bias, and personnel training of the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, Acting Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.summary: Sebald reports Japanese officials' view that a Europe- and China-oriented clique under Katsuo Okazaki dominates the Foreign Ministry and neglects American affairs.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1448 (1445) on Present Organization of the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs

subfiles.about: A detailed organizational roster and staffing breakdown of the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs listing personnel counts, bureau and section chiefs, deputies, and duties.
subfiles.from: Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.summary: Organization of Japan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs: 898 staff across its bureaus, Secretariat and Training Institute.
subfiles.title: Enclosure to Despatch No. 1445: Present Organization of the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs

subfiles.about: A confidential despatch reporting the impending resignation of Chester W. Hepler as Chief of SCAP's Labor Division over occupation labor policy disagreements.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.summary: Sebald reports Chester W. Hepler, SCAP Labor Division chief, is resigning, believing SCAP policies aggravated relations with Japanese labor; he joins the ILO.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 498 on the Pending Resignation of Chester W. Hepler, Chief of SCAP Labor Division
